newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic access lines grew 3.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic access lines grew 3.8 percent.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp said access lines in service on December 31 grew 3.8 percent to 20.6 million from a year before, while access minutes of use grew 9.7 percent.
The company said the growth includes 12.9 percent year-over-year Centrex line growth in business markets.
Bell Atlantic earlier reported lower fourth quarter earnings on higher total operating revenues. Its 1996 year earnings grew slightly despite lower operating revenues.
Bell Atlantic said that net grew 10 percent to $1.87 billion from $1.70 billion a year earlier if one-time items in the year and quarter are excluded.
On a per share basis earnings excluding one-time items were $0.97 per share, identical to First Call's analyst consensus, compared with $0.90 reported a year earlier.
The company said fourth quarter operating revenues for the core business rose 7.9 percent and adjusted network revenues rose 6.0 percent from a year earlier.
It said about 200,000 integrated services digital network (ISDN) lines were in service at December 31, up 39 percent from the year-ago total.

Bell Atlantic said annual subscriber growth for Bell Atlantic NYNEX Mobile was 31 percent, with a million new customers bringing the total to just over 4.4 million. This included around a million customers for Talk-Along and EZ-Max.
Revenues from so-called vertical services like caller ID, call waiting and home voice mail grew 23 percent from a year earlier, Bell Atlantic said.
"We posted strong gains in our key communication markets in 1996 as we prepare to complete our merger with NYNEX," said Bell Atlantic chief executive Raymond Smith.
The company expects to complete its merger with NYNEX Corp towards the end of the current quarter.
